overview: This report covers 18 unseen announcements: 5 HIGH PRIORITY, 8 RELATED / POSSIBLY INTERESTING, and 5 LOW PRIORITY. Central connections include full-shift factors in parabolic responses, topological linearization, periodic-point asymptotics, approximate-group orbit counting and Cantor odometer actions. Related work concerns intermittent invariant measures, homoclinic structures, Anosov resonances, invariant-measure contraction bounds, geometric quotients and arithmetic hitting times. No followed-author matches occur; unnamed hypotheses, conditional conclusions and numerical observations retain their stated qualifications.

paper.title: Doubly Intermittent Singular Skew Products
paper.abstract: We study a large class of skew product systems, which can also be thought of as random dynamical systems, coupling a uniformly expanding circle map with a full branch interval map with two indifferent fixed points and unbounded derivatives. This significantly generalizes the setting of several skew products considered in the literature, in particular the Gou\"ezel skew products [Gou\"ezel, Statistical properties of a skew product with a curve of neutral points, Erg. Th. & Dyn. Sys. (2007)], in which the fibre maps are intermittency maps with a single indifferent fixed point and bounded derivatives. Through the construction of an induced full branch map, we prove various statistical properties of the skew products, including existence of an invariant probability measure equivalent to Lebesgue and decay of correlations.

analysis.relevance_note: An invariant probability equivalent to Lebesgue and correlation decay connect this intermittent skew-product setting to invariant-measure dynamics.
analysis.tldr: An induced full-branch construction yields invariant-measure and statistical results for skew products with two indifferent fibre fixed points and unbounded derivatives.
analysis.problem: Study statistical properties of skew products coupling an expanding circle map to doubly intermittent interval maps.
analysis.main_result: For a large class coupling a uniformly expanding circle map with a full-branch interval map having two indifferent fixed points and unbounded derivatives, the authors prove existence of an invariant probability measure equivalent to Lebesgue and decay of correlations. The setting generalizes skew products whose fibre maps have one indifferent fixed point and bounded derivatives. The exact admissibility assumptions and correlation-decay rate: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Construction of an induced full-branch map
analysis.context: Intermittency, skew products, random dynamical systems and statistical properties.

paper.title: Realization of expanding dynamics by a finite horizon parabolic law response
paper.abstract: We study the discrete dynamical system generated by iterating an episodic response of a population density. In each episode, the running potential is frozen at the current density, agents solve a quadratic control problem, and the terminal density is passed to the next episode. For each prescribed positive horizon $\tau$ and each $C^k$ map $F$ of finitely many Fourier moments, with $1\le k<\infty$, we construct a finite mode interaction realizing $F$ at order $\varepsilon$. In scaled coordinates, the exact parabolic response satisfies $\|T^{(d)}_{\varepsilon,\tau}-(F,S(\tau)|_{\Es_d})\|_{C^k}\le C\varepsilon$. The estimate is uniform over a full bounded infinite dimensional Sobolev fibre and needs neither Fourier truncation nor an invariant manifold. For scalar targets with disjoint expanding branches that strictly cover their convex hull, this $C^1$ control and parabolic compactness yield compact invariant sets of the exact response. These sets factor onto the full one sided shift and contain periodic densities of every least period. Nondegenerate periodic orbits continue, and hyperbolicity requires a separate strict multiplier condition. We also prove a derivative cost obstruction for nonaffine microscopic realization, a susceptibility weighted criterion for population energy designs, and the failure of exact scalar closure under nontrivial rank one feedback. The results concern designed frozen law responses, not Nash consistent mean field game equilibria or finite player limits.

analysis.relevance_note: A full one-sided shift factor and periodic densities of every least period make symbolic dynamics central, despite the parabolic control setting.
analysis.tldr: Designed frozen-law parabolic responses realize prescribed finite-moment maps to first order and, for suitable expanding scalar targets, admit full-shift factors.
analysis.problem: Realize finite-dimensional dynamics by iterating a finite-horizon episodic population-density response.
analysis.main_result: For every prescribed horizon \(\tau>0\) and every \(C^k\) map of finitely many Fourier moments, with \(1\leq k<\infty\), a finite-mode interaction realizes that map at order \(\varepsilon\). In scaled coordinates the exact response is \(C^k\)-within \(C\varepsilon\) of the target coupled with the stated semigroup action on the complementary fibre, uniformly over a full bounded infinite-dimensional Sobolev fibre, without truncation or an invariant manifold. For scalar targets with disjoint expanding branches strictly covering their convex hull, \(C^1\) control and parabolic compactness yield compact invariant sets factoring onto the full one-sided shift and containing periodic densities of every least period. Nondegenerate periodic orbits continue; hyperbolicity needs a separate strict multiplier condition. Further results give a derivative-cost obstruction for nonaffine microscopic realization, a susceptibility-weighted energy-design criterion, and failure of exact scalar closure under nontrivial rank-one feedback. These are designed frozen-law responses, not Nash-consistent mean field game equilibria or finite-player limits. The multiplier condition and other explicit criteria: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Symbolic factors and periodic dynamics in iterated parabolic population responses.

paper.title: Spatial switching near a four-loop homoclinic bouquet: a mechanism for multi-bump bound states in coupled nonlinear Schr\"odinger systems
paper.abstract: We study how a localized standing wave of a coupled nonlinear Schr\"odinger (CNLS) system can switch between components from one pulse to the next. The standing wave reduction of the CNLS system yields a four-dimensional Hamiltonian system with two reflection symmetries, in which four elementary pulses correspond to a bouquet of homoclinic loops to a saddle. For saddle eigenvalues $\pm\lambda_{1},\pm\lambda_{2}$ satisfying $0<\lambda_{1} < \lambda_{2} < 2\lambda_1$, and under suitable nondegeneracy assumptions, we construct stable and unstable invariant manifolds of the four-loop bouquet. Apart from trajectories asymptotic to the saddle in the corresponding time direction, these manifolds characterize one-sided trapping near the bouquet within the critical Hamiltonian level, namely the level set containing the saddle equilibrium. Both manifolds have codimension one in this level. We prove that if they intersect transversely away from the bouquet, producing super-homoclinic orbits, then there exist infinitely many multi-bump homoclinic orbits to the saddle. These orbits correspond to multi-bump localized standing waves of the CNLS system.

analysis.relevance_note: Invariant manifolds, transverse homoclinic intersections and infinitely many multi-bump orbits give a substantial hyperbolic-dynamics connection.
analysis.tldr: Under eigenvalue and nondegeneracy assumptions, transverse intersections of bouquet invariant manifolds force infinitely many multi-bump homoclinic standing waves.
analysis.problem: Describe pulse-to-pulse component switching near a four-loop homoclinic bouquet in coupled nonlinear Schrödinger standing waves.
analysis.main_result: The standing-wave reduction is a four-dimensional Hamiltonian system with two reflection symmetries and four elementary pulses forming homoclinic loops to a saddle. For saddle eigenvalues \(\pm\lambda_1,\pm\lambda_2\) with \(0<\lambda_1<\lambda_2<2\lambda_1\), and suitable nondegeneracy assumptions, stable and unstable invariant manifolds of the bouquet are constructed. Both have codimension one in the critical Hamiltonian level. Except for trajectories asymptotic to the saddle in the corresponding time direction, they characterize one-sided trapping near the bouquet in that level. If the manifolds meet transversely away from the bouquet, producing super-homoclinic orbits, infinitely many multi-bump homoclinic orbits follow, corresponding to localized standing waves. The nondegeneracy assumptions: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Construction of stable and unstable invariant manifolds
analysis.context: Homoclinic dynamics and multi-pulse standing waves in coupled nonlinear Schrödinger systems.

paper.title: Linearization for unbounded perturbations of sublinear growth
paper.abstract: We investigate global topological linearization with unbounded perturbations of sublinear growth. Under a spectral gap condition and a sufficiently small Lipschitz constant, we show that the displacements of both the conjugacy and its inverse from the identity satisfy the same growth bound as the perturbation. Moreover, the conjugacy is unique within the class of maps whose displacements satisfy this bound. We obtain representations of the displacement in terms of stable and unstable orbit series that converge uniformly on any bounded set and give the inverse conjugacy by using the Banach fixed points theorem in a weighted function space.

analysis.relevance_note: Global topological conjugacy, its uniqueness and its growth control directly concern topological classification of dynamics.
analysis.tldr: A spectral gap and a small Lipschitz constant give global topological linearization with matching sublinear displacement bounds for the conjugacy and its inverse.
analysis.problem: Control and uniquely characterize conjugacies for unbounded perturbations of sublinear growth.
analysis.main_result: Under a spectral gap condition and a sufficiently small Lipschitz constant, both the conjugacy and its inverse differ from the identity by displacements satisfying the same growth bound as the perturbation. The conjugacy is unique within the class satisfying that displacement bound. Stable and unstable orbit-series representations converge uniformly on every bounded set, and the inverse conjugacy is obtained using the Banach fixed point theorem in a weighted function space. The precise spectral gap, smallness threshold and underlying linear system: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Banach fixed point theorem in a weighted function space
analysis.context: Global topological linearization and growth-controlled conjugacy.

paper.title: Saddle-focus to saddle transition of 4D heteroclinic orbits resembling oscillatory and regularized shock waves of some dissipative Boussinesq systems
paper.abstract: Oscillatory and regularized shock waves have long been studied to understand the formation and dynamics of undular bores in shallow waters, phenomena that typically arise from the interplay between dispersion, nonlinearity, and dissipation. In this work, we investigate and describe the nature and shape of traveling wave solutions that resemble oscillatory and regularized shock waves of some Boussinesq-type water wave models known as Bona--Smith systems in the presence of dissipation. The associated traveling wave equations are solutions of four-dimensional dynamical systems, leading to both computational challenges and rich structural behavior. In particular, to describe the properties of these traveling waves, we analyze heteroclinic orbits that connect two distinct equilibria, one of which undergoes a transition in the four-dimensional phase space from a saddle-focus to a saddle point as the dissipation parameter increases. This transition governs the nature of the wave profile, which evolves smoothly from an oscillatory shock wave to a regularized (non-oscillatory) shock wave. To compute such solutions, we introduce a finite-difference-based numerical method tailored for this class of problems.

analysis.relevance_note: Numerical traveling-wave analysis for dissipative water-wave models has no central entropy, symbolic or dimension-theoretic component in the abstract.

paper.title: Dissipative Geometric Flows and Certified Phase-Volume Contraction
paper.abstract: This paper develops an approach to uniform phase-volume contraction for prescribed dynamical systems. The main result is that every positive rate strictly below the invariant-measure bound can be certified in finite search time by a regularized Sobolev gradient flow. The resulting positive density ensures exponential contraction of the weighted phase volume with unit prefactor. For each fixed regularization parameter, the flow converges exponentially to a unique minimizer. As the regularization vanishes, these minimizers converge to the feasible potential of minimum Sobolev norm for a fixed feasibility margin. The certification procedure rests on a Holder estimate that converts a bound on the integral penalty into a pointwise bound on the weighted divergence over the entire invariant domain. This estimate yields a stopping criterion for the search. Finite termination is also established in growing finite-dimensional trial spaces for a staged scheme with exact gradient evaluations and controlled positive quadrature. The scheme requires neither a supplied feasibility margin nor a bound on the norm of a feasible potential. A disk example shows that the invariant-measure bound can be approached by smooth certificates even when no C^1 certificate attains it. Analytical properties of novel local D-Liouville, D-Yamabe, and D-Ricci evolutions driven by divergence penalties are established. For the unnormalized D-Yamabe flow, a scaling obstruction to exponential stability of stationary conformal factors is established. For the D-Ricci flow, the transformation law for the prescribed vector field under DeTurck pullback is derived. This law specifies how the vector field must transform when the gauge term is removed. Examples on the torus and sphere identify obstructions to smooth convergence of the geometric evolutions.

analysis.relevance_note: An invariant-measure bound governing uniform contraction certificates gives a clear connection to invariant-measure optimization, although entropy and dimension are not addressed.
analysis.tldr: Regularized Sobolev gradient flows certify every positive phase-volume contraction rate strictly below the invariant-measure bound in finite search time.
analysis.problem: Find positive densities certifying uniform weighted phase-volume contraction and analyze divergence-driven geometric evolutions.
analysis.main_result: Every positive rate strictly below the invariant-measure bound can be certified in finite search time by a regularized Sobolev gradient flow, yielding exponential contraction of weighted phase volume with unit prefactor. For fixed regularization the flow converges exponentially to a unique minimizer; as regularization vanishes, minimizers converge to the feasible potential of minimum Sobolev norm for a fixed feasibility margin. A Hölder estimate converts an integral penalty bound to a pointwise weighted-divergence bound and gives a stopping criterion. A staged scheme in growing finite-dimensional trial spaces also terminates with exact gradient evaluations and controlled positive quadrature, without a supplied feasibility margin or feasible-potential norm bound. A disk example permits smooth certificates approaching the bound without an attaining continuously differentiable certificate. Further results identify an unnormalized D-Yamabe scaling obstruction, the prescribed-field transformation under D-Ricci DeTurck pullback, and torus/sphere obstructions to smooth convergence. The invariant-measure bound formula and precise regularity hypotheses: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Invariant-measure bounds, weighted divergence and dissipative geometric flows.

paper.title: Twisted Poincar\'e series at zero on surfaces
paper.abstract: Let $(\Sigma,g)$ be a closed, connected, oriented, Riemannian Anosov surface. We show that there exists an open subset $\mathcal V_g$ of the space of finite-dimensional irreducible representations of the fundamental group of $\Sigma$, whose complement has complex codimension at least one, such that the following holds: for all $x,y\in \Sigma$, $\rho \in \mathcal{V}_g$, the meromorphic extension of the twisted Poincar\'e series $s \mapsto \eta_{g,\rho,x,y}(s)$ vanishes at $s=0$. We also give examples of non-trivial representations whose Poincar\'e series does not vanish at zero. In addition, we describe the structure of twisted resonant states at zero for these examples and show that they admit non-trivial Jordan blocks.

analysis.relevance_note: Twisted Poincaré series and zero resonances on Anosov surfaces connect hyperbolic dynamics with spectral structure.
analysis.tldr: Twisted Poincaré series vanish at zero on a large open representation locus, while exceptional nontrivial representations give nonvanishing and nontrivial Jordan blocks.
analysis.problem: Determine zero values of meromorphically continued twisted Poincaré series and the corresponding resonant states.
analysis.main_result: For a closed, connected, oriented Riemannian Anosov surface \((\Sigma,g)\), an open subset \(\mathcal V_g\) of finite-dimensional irreducible representations of its fundamental group has complement of complex codimension at least one. For every \(x,y\in\Sigma\) and every \(\rho\in\mathcal V_g\), the meromorphic extension of \(s\mapsto\eta_{g,\rho,x,y}(s)\) vanishes at \(s=0\). Examples of nontrivial representations have a Poincaré series not vanishing at zero; their twisted resonant states at zero are described and admit nontrivial Jordan blocks. The proof methods: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Anosov surfaces, twisted Poincaré series and resonances.

paper.title: Counting periodic points of rational self-maps of projective varieties
paper.abstract: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the number of isolated periodic points of a dominant rational self-map of a smooth projective variety. We first give an upper bound for this number in terms of the degrees of the iterates of the map, thereby extending a theorem of Dinh--Nguyen--Truong to arbitrary characteristic. Our approach is purely algebraic and bypasses the theory of densities of positive closed currents. We then establish the exact asymptotic growth of isolated periodic points of birational self-maps of surfaces over a field of characteristic 0. To do so, we extend Jonsson--Reschke's argument to any finitely generated field over $ \mathbb Q $ using Moriwaki's theory of heights.

analysis.relevance_note: Asymptotic growth of isolated periodic points is a central orbit-complexity question.
analysis.tldr: Algebraic methods bound isolated periodic-point counts in arbitrary characteristic and give exact asymptotic growth for birational surface maps in characteristic zero.
analysis.problem: Count isolated periodic points of dominant rational self-maps of smooth projective varieties.
analysis.main_result: An upper bound in terms of degrees of iterates extends the cited Dinh–Nguyen–Truong theorem to arbitrary characteristic, using a purely algebraic approach. For birational self-maps of surfaces over a characteristic-zero field, the authors establish exact asymptotic growth of isolated periodic points. They extend the cited Jonsson–Reschke argument to any finitely generated field over \(\mathbb Q\) using Moriwaki height theory. The explicit upper bound, asymptotic formula and any further hypotheses: Not specified in the abstract.

paper.title: Elimination Methods for Computing Invariant Algebraic Surfaces and Hopf Bifurcations
paper.abstract: This paper presents efficient algorithmic methods for computing invariant algebraic surfaces and Hopf bifurcations in parametric polynomial differential systems. For invariant algebraic surfaces of bounded degree, we establish two complementary elimination frameworks: combining Gr\"obner bases with saturation and prime decomposition yields the Zariski closure of the parameter existence locus (necessary conditions), whereas triangular decomposition into strong regular systems recovers the exact pointwise constructible locus (necessary and sufficient conditions) via the projection property. We further present a hybrid approach for identifying such surfaces by integrating prime decomposition with branch-wise triangular solving, thereby efficiently deriving necessary and sufficient conditions with enhanced computational flexibility and rectifying subtle classification errors in a class of Li\'enard systems. For Hopf bifurcations, extending prior work on necessary conditions [SIAM J. Numer. Anal. 34 (1997)] and sufficient conditions [J. Math. Anal. Appl. 182 (1994); J. Symbolic Comput. 30 (2000)], we establish a complete algebraic characterization via two equivalent formulations: one using Hurwitz determinants and subresultant sequences, and another derived from the greatest common divisor (GCD) of the real and imaginary parts of the characteristic polynomial. From the GCD formulation, we obtain a novel and, for the first time, complete semi-algebraic description of the transversality condition, yielding a decision procedure via triangular decomposition of semi-algebraic systems and heuristic real quantifier elimination. Our approach resolves cases beyond the reach of state-of-the-art polynomial-based methods, and experimental results confirm the feasibility and efficiency of our frameworks.

analysis.relevance_note: Algebraic algorithms for invariant surfaces and Hopf bifurcations lack a central connection to the strongest research interests in the supplied abstract.

paper.title: On the invertibility of saddle-point matrices: exact algebraic conditions and applications to constrained dynamics
paper.abstract: The solvability of constrained dynamical systems governed by D'Alembert--Lagrange mechanics relies directly on the invertibility of the coefficient matrix describing the underlying saddle-point structure, which couples system inertia with kinematic constraints. Standard formulations often rely on overly restrictive sufficient assumptions, such as global positive definiteness or semi-definiteness of the mass matrix, frequently combined with generalized inverses to handle singular mass distributions. In this work, we establish the purely necessary and sufficient algebraic conditions for matrix invertibility: the kinematic independence of the constraints and a kernel intersection condition between the allowed directions of motion and the induced inertial forces. We provide a physical interpretation of this requirement, demonstrating that it eliminates non-zero admissible motions whose generated inertial forces are entirely absorbed by constraint reactions. Furthermore, by completely avoiding generalized inverses, this formulation offers a unified and coordinate-free framework capable of handling massless components and indefinite inertia structures within a computationally robust setting.

analysis.relevance_note: Saddle-point matrix invertibility in constrained mechanics is mainly an algebraic solvability problem without a central dynamics-profile connection.

paper.title: Smale's Mean Values And Geometric Mean Values
paper.abstract: We prove that, for every integer $d>2$ and every $L>0$, there exists a polynomial of degree $d$ whose geometric mean value exceeds $L$. This result demonstrates that the geometric mean value alone is insufficient to establish the smallest upper bound for the minimum of Smale's mean values. Under certain additional assumptions, we derive upper bounds for the geometric mean value, thereby verifying Smale's mean value conjecture for several subclasses of polynomials. Furthermore, we connect Smale's mean values to Fekete points. Motivated by this connection, we formulate a new problem concerning Fekete points in the spirit of Smale's mean values.

analysis.relevance_note: Polynomial mean-value bounds and their Fekete-point connection are indirectly related to complex-dynamical interests; the abstract gives no explicit entropy or dimension result.
analysis.tldr: Geometric mean values are unbounded for every polynomial degree greater than two, while additional assumptions yield bounds verifying Smale’s conjecture in several subclasses.
analysis.problem: Assess geometric mean values as a route to sharp bounds for the minimum of Smale’s mean values.
analysis.main_result: For every integer \(d>2\) and every \(L>0\), there is a degree-\(d\) polynomial whose geometric mean value exceeds \(L\). Thus the geometric mean alone cannot establish the smallest upper bound for the minimum of Smale’s mean values. Under additional assumptions the authors obtain upper bounds and verify Smale’s mean value conjecture for several polynomial subclasses. They connect these mean values to Fekete points and formulate a related new problem. The definitions, additional assumptions, subclass descriptions and quantitative upper bounds: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Polynomial mean-value problems and Fekete points.

paper.title: Strong convergence rate for non-autonomous slow-fast SDEs driven by Brownian motions and {\alpha}-stable processes
paper.abstract:
In this paper, we establish a quantitative strong averaging principle for a class of time quasi-periodic slow-fast stochastic differential equations driven by both Brownian motions and multiplicative $\alpha$-stable L'evy processes. We show that the slow component converges strongly to an autonomous averaged equation with rate $\varepsilon^{\min\{1-1/\alpha_2,\,1/(
u+2)\}}$, where $\alpha_2\in(1,2)$ is the fast stability index and $
u$ comes from the quasi-periodic structure. Our strategy is as follows. We first derive the intermediate step of the averaging principle to average out the effect of fast-variable oscillations on the system, although the averaged variable still depends on $\varepsilon$. We obtain the convergence rate $\varepsilon^{1-1/\alpha_2}$. Furthermore, under the uniformly quasi-periodic conditions, we show that the slow component converges strongly to the solution of some autonomous averaged equation, whose coefficients independent of $\varepsilon$. We thus obtain the convergence rate $\varepsilon^{1/(
u+2)}$. The main contribution of this paper is to extend the additive L'evy noise to multiplicative L'evy noise and extend the fast equation of the system from the autonomous setting to the non-autonomous setting. In particular, we establish an explicit convergence rate in the quasi-periodic setting, extending the corresponding results for the periodic case.

analysis.relevance_note: Quantitative stochastic averaging for slow-fast equations is not centrally connected to entropy, symbolic dynamics, fractal dimension or group actions here.

paper.title: Quasiperiodicity breakdown and homoclinic bifurcations in the forced librations of a parametric oscillator
paper.abstract: Above its instability threshold, a parametrically excited oscillator settles into one of two phase states. The response of these states to a second, much slower modulation of the same stiffness is investigated. In the rotating frame, this modulation periodically varies the detuning and drives the phase librations. When the modulation is slow compared with the libration frequency, the phase states follow adiabatically. As the two frequencies become comparable, this approximation breaks down and the driven libration resonates with the intrinsic one. This nonadiabatic regime is examined for a Duffing oscillator with nonlinear damping. The averaged equations describe a periodically perturbed planar system with integrable unperturbed dynamics, whose homoclinic loop is derived in closed form. The phase states persist as invariant tori supporting quasiperiodic motion. Their stability and period-doubling bifurcations are captured by a damped Mathieu equation, in which the modulation contributes to both parametric stiffness and parametric damping. A Melnikov analysis yields explicit thresholds for separatrix splitting and the onset of homoclinic intersections, which are corroborated by numerical computations of the invariant manifolds. Numerically it is revealed that these intersections arise well before sustained chaotic motion develops. The fate of the parametric oscillation depends markedly on the resonance condition: modulation at the libration frequency destroys the invariant tori and quenches the oscillation, whereas modulation at twice the libration frequency leaves it intact.

analysis.relevance_note: Invariant tori, separatrix splitting and analytically studied homoclinic intersections provide a smooth-dynamics connection beyond the oscillator application.
analysis.tldr: Averaging, Mathieu stability analysis and Melnikov thresholds describe forced-libration bifurcations, with numerical evidence separating homoclinic intersections from sustained chaos.
analysis.problem: Determine how slow stiffness modulation affects the two phase states of a parametrically excited oscillator.
analysis.main_result: For a Duffing oscillator with nonlinear damping in the nonadiabatic regime, averaged equations form a periodically perturbed planar system with integrable unperturbed dynamics and an explicit homoclinic loop. Phase states persist as invariant tori with quasiperiodic motion. A damped Mathieu equation captures stability and period doubling, with modulation affecting both stiffness and damping. Melnikov analysis gives explicit separatrix-splitting and homoclinic-intersection thresholds, corroborated by numerical invariant manifolds. Numerically, intersections appear well before sustained chaotic motion. Modulation at the libration frequency destroys the tori and quenches oscillation, whereas twice-frequency modulation leaves the oscillation intact. The exact parameter conditions and threshold formulas: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Quasiperiodic invariant tori and homoclinic bifurcations in forced librations.

paper.title: Patterson-Sullivan Theory for Approximate Groups
paper.abstract: In this paper we consider the limit set of a uniformly discrete approximate subgroup acting on a negatively curved manifold, and prove several properties comparable to that of the classical case of discrete groups, including a version of the dichotomy between elementary and non-elementary groups. Furthermore, we adapt the Patterson-Sullivan construction for discrete groups to obtain asymptotic counting results for the orbits of infinite uniformly discrete approximate groups acting on a negatively curved manifold.

analysis.relevance_note: Approximate-group actions, their limit sets and asymptotic orbit counting directly match group-action and orbit-complexity interests.
analysis.tldr: Patterson–Sullivan constructions extend to infinite uniformly discrete approximate groups acting on negatively curved manifolds and yield orbit-counting asymptotics.
analysis.problem: Develop limit-set and orbit-counting theory for uniformly discrete approximate subgroups in negative curvature.
analysis.main_result: For a uniformly discrete approximate subgroup acting on a negatively curved manifold, the authors establish limit-set properties comparable to the discrete-group case, including a version of the elementary/non-elementary dichotomy. An adaptation of the Patterson–Sullivan construction gives asymptotic counting results for orbits of infinite uniformly discrete approximate groups acting on negatively curved manifolds. The precise counting formula, further geometric assumptions and any dimension statement: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Approximate-group actions, negative curvature and limit-set geometry.

paper.title: A smooth compactification of similarity classes of triangles
paper.abstract: We provide a smooth algebraic compactification of the space of labeled, oriented similarity classes of triangles, as a quotient of a 3-point configuration space in the plane -- minus triple-collisions -- by the similarity group. The configuration space is naturally isomorphic to the Fulton-MacPherson space of \cite{FM94} and to the Schubert-Semple space of \cite{Semple}. The quotient is topologically a connected sum of three projective planes, and projects via blow-down to two shape spaces that have appeared in the literature: the well-known 2-sphere (\cite{Kend84}, \cite{Beh}, \cite{Montgomery}, \cite{ES15}), and the less-well-known 2-torus (\cite{BG23}). A natural action by the dihedral group $D_6$ yields a quotient stack describing absolute (unlabeled, unoriented) triangle classes.

analysis.relevance_note: Similarity-group and dihedral-group quotients give a topological group-action connection, although the main object is a geometric compactification rather than orbit complexity.
analysis.tldr: Triangle similarity classes admit a smooth algebraic compactification with topology given by a connected sum of three projective planes and a dihedral quotient stack.
analysis.problem: Compactify labeled, oriented triangle similarity classes and relate them to absolute triangle classes.
analysis.main_result: The compactification is a quotient by the similarity group of a three-point planar configuration space with triple collisions removed. That configuration space is naturally isomorphic to the cited Fulton–MacPherson and Schubert–Semple spaces. The quotient is topologically a connected sum of three projective planes and projects by blow-down to a two-sphere and a two-torus shape space. A natural \(D_6\) action yields a quotient stack describing unlabeled, unoriented triangle classes. The detailed smooth construction and action formulas: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Similarity-group quotient of a configuration space
analysis.context: Triangle shape spaces, compactification and group quotients.

paper.title: The Subtractive Divisor Orbit: Unconditional Bounds, Parity Constraints, and a Conditional Framework
paper.abstract: Let $a(n)$ be the number of iterations of $F(m)=m-\tau(m)$ needed to reach zero, where $\tau(m)$ counts the positive divisors of $m$. Write $\Delta(n)=a(n)-a(n-1)$. We prove that for every $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large $X$, each of the inequalities $\Delta(n)\ge X^{1/2-\varepsilon}$ and $\Delta(n)\le -X^{1/2-\varepsilon}$ holds for at least $X^{1-\varepsilon}$ integers $1\le n\le X$. The proof uses the identity $F(2m)=2F(m)$ at odd $m$ and the fact that an odd orbit first changes parity at a square. For every fixed $C>0$, a positive proportion of starting values $n\in(X,4X]$ satisfy $\left|a(n)-\frac{Cn}{\log n}\right|\gg_C\frac{\sqrt X}{\log X}$. For the hitting time itself we prove $a(x)\ll_b\frac{x}{(\log x)^b}$ for every $b<\log 2$, together with a lower bound having logarithmic exponent $2.988206\ldots$. On complete crossings of $(N,2N]$, with $Z=2N$, the logarithm of the step size has normal order $(\log 2)\log\log Z$, uniformly in the starting value. Computations through $10^9$ give the largest positive and negative first differences in this range.

analysis.relevance_note: Quantitative hitting times and orbit-step statistics provide an indirect discrete orbit-complexity connection, without an entropy or dimension claim.
analysis.tldr: The subtractive divisor iteration has large first differences of both signs, quantitative hitting-time bounds and a normal-order statement for step sizes.
analysis.problem: Bound the hitting time and its fluctuations for iteration of the subtractive divisor map.
analysis.main_result: Let \(F(m)=m-\tau(m)\), where \(\tau\) counts positive divisors, let \(a(n)\) be the number of iterations to zero, and set \(\Delta(n)=a(n)-a(n-1)\). For every \(\varepsilon>0\) and sufficiently large \(X\), each of \(\Delta(n)\geq X^{1/2-\varepsilon}\) and \(\Delta(n)\leq-X^{1/2-\varepsilon}\) holds for at least \(X^{1-\varepsilon}\) integers in \([1,X]\). For every fixed \(C>0\), a positive proportion of \(n\in(X,4X]\) satisfy \(\lvert a(n)-Cn/\log n\rvert\gg_C\sqrt X/\log X\). Also \(a(x)\ll_b x/(\log x)^b\) for every \(b<\log2\), with a lower bound having logarithmic exponent \(2.988206\ldots\). On complete crossings of \((N,2N]\), with \(Z=2N\), the logarithm of the step size has normal order \((\log2)\log\log Z\), uniformly in starting value. Computations through \(10^9\) give extreme first differences. The complete lower-bound formula and any conditional-framework assumptions: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: First parity change of an odd orbit at a square
analysis.context: Arithmetic iteration, hitting times and parity constraints.

paper.title: LLM-ACES: Closed-Loop Discovery of Dynamical Systems with LLM-Guided Adaptive Search
paper.abstract: Recovering governing ordinary differential equations (ODEs) from data is a central challenge in modeling dynamical systems across scientific domains. Existing approaches cast discovery as a static inference problem over fixed datasets, assuming that the observed trajectories are sufficiently informative. However, dynamical systems evolve over large state spaces, and limited data can make multiple equations observationally indistinguishable, leading to identifiability gaps and the recovery of incorrect governing equations. To address this, we introduce LLM-ACES, or LLM-guided Active Closed-loop Equation Search, a closed-loop framework that jointly optimizes symbolic hypothesis construction and adaptive data acquisition. In LLM-ACES, a large language model (LLM) proposes operator priors that define constrained subspaces of the symbolic search space, within which candidate equations are fit to the observed data. The disagreement among these candidates guides the acquisition of informative trajectories, creating a feedback loop that iteratively refines both the hypothesis space and the discovered dynamics. On 122 ODE systems spanning ODEBench and ODEBase, LLM-ACES achieves the lowest median NMSE, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines while reaching the highest symbolic accuracy up to 70.8% on ODEBench and 69.5% on ODEBase across different LLM backbones. Our analysis further shows that LLM-ACES is sample-efficient, achieving better performance with less data. Under observation noise and sparse sampling, LLM-ACES keeps the lowest reconstruction error without inflating expression complexity, whereas baselines tend to add spurious terms that fit the data locally but obscure the governing relationships. Code: https://github.com/scientific-discovery/LLM-ACES

paper.title: Nonnuclear Bunce-Deddens algebras
paper.abstract: We introduce nonnuclear Bunce-Deddens algebras, defined as reduced crossed product C*-algebras associated with free odometer actions of nonamenable countable discrete residually finite groups on a Cantor space. These are nonnuclear counterparts to the generalised Bunce-Deddens algebras introduced by Orfanos. For large classes of groups, we show that they share many regularity properties, including real rank zero, stable rank one, strict comparison of positive elements, and admitting a unique tracial state. In many cases, we deduce that they are even selfless and hence pure. Finally, we compute the ordered K-theory and trace pairing of Bunce-Deddens algebras over nonabelian free groups.
